US Navy single-base smokeless powder, diphenylamine stabilized (adopted 1908).
Effective definition calibrated to reproduce 16in/50 Mk7 full-charge service ballistics: 2700 lb Mk8 APCBC, 660 lb charge, 762 m/s at 18.5 long ton/in2 peak breech.
Force, covolume and gamma adopted from single-base NC literature; burn-rate coefficient calibrated, pressure exponent assumed 0.949.
Web-size estimator (grain web from gun geometry; travel-length convention): web[mm] = 0.263*(travel/MV[ms])^0.97 * ld^0.64, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]; expansion-ratio factor dropped (collinear with ld, r=0.97). Leave-one-out CV 4.6%. Apply a 0.5 mm web floor: below it the grain burns out in <5% of travel (web becomes ballistically meaningless) and it is finer than the smallest historical web (SPD 5in/25, 0.72 mm). This floor only binds for SPD on small or short-barrel guns; the cordite estimators clear it on their own.
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = charge[kg]/0.65 for standard guns (loading density ~0.65 kg/dm3, charge exponent ~1, LOO-CV ~4%); the three 8in cruiser guns are oversized-chamber outliers (~0.46 kg/dm3) that inflate a blanket fit to rho 0.58 / 20%. Exhaustive log-log search over charge, caliber, shell, MV, travel and bore-volume finds NO term that captures the 8in anomaly - it is a localized design trait, not a smooth function of gun parameters (an additive fit that looks better is an absolute-error artifact, +100-180% on the 5in guns). Charge-free fallback: chamber = 1.4e-9*shell[kg]^0.97*MV[m/s]^2.97 (LOO 30%).

RN double-base cordite, Modified (adopted 1901): 65% nitrocellulose / 30% nitroglycerin / 5% mineral jelly.
Force from cordite literature: heat of explosion ~1020 cal/g (water liquid) -> Q_v ~4.0 MJ/kg; F = (gamma-1)*Q_v ~1.04 MJ/kg.
Validated against the RN 15in/42 Mk I in cord form (solid-cylinder grain, SimpleGeometry.CYLINDER): 869.5 kg shell, 194 kg charge -> 752 m/s at ~312 MPa. Reproduced under the full-bore-length convention (length_gun = bore length), which supplies the expansion this low-load-density (386 kg/m3) gun needs; under travel geometry the model is efficiency-limited and over-demands force.
Burn-rate coefficient calibrated to known MD cord diameters (5.5in/50 -> MD19 = 4.83 mm; 6in/50 Mk XI/XIII/XVII -> MD26 = 6.60 mm; 12in/45 Mk X -> MD45 = 11.43 mm): u_1 = 9.5e-9 reproduces these cords when web is fit to MV (6in/50 within 0-3%), where the prior 8.0e-9 (from MV-only fits) gave cords ~15-30% thin. Pressure fit is unchanged (u_1-invariant under web-to-MV fitting). Force needs no gradient (unlike SC): per-gun force at the real cords clusters at 1.03 +/- 0.04 MJ/kg with no load-density trend, confirming the thermochemical 1.04.
Web-size estimator (full-bore convention): web[mm] = 31.8*(travel/MV[ms])^0.92 * E^-1.11 * ld^2.03, E = (chamber+bore-swept)/chamber, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]. Leave-one-out CV 11.5%; validated against the 5 real cords (RMS 10%). Shared 0.5 mm web floor (defined under SPD) never binds for MD - predictions stay well above 1 mm.
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = charge[kg]/0.42 (loading density ~0.42 kg/dm3, charge exponent ~1, LOO-CV 10%). Exhaustive search (charge, caliber, shell, MV, travel, bore-volume): the best multi-term (charge*travel, LOO 8.6%) is a collinearity ridge - charge and travel correlate at r=0.98 - so no robust term improves it. One mild outlier, the 9.2in/31.5 Mk III (oversized chamber, ratio 3.0 - originally sized for prismatic brown powder, then loaded with denser cordite); dropping it tightens the charge rule to LOO 7.2%. Charge-free fallback: chamber = 1.9e-13*caliber[mm]^3.38*MV[m/s]^2.33 (LOO 21%).

RN solventless cordite (adopted 1927): 49.5% nitrocellulose / 41.5% nitroglycerin / 9% centralite.
Headline force 1.02 MJ/kg, validated full-bore/cord against RN guns 4in-16in: reproduces the 15in/42 (SC280) and 14in/45 (SC300) within ~2%, and fits an 11-gun fleet to RMS ~9% on working pressure (web fit to MV).
Best fleet fit uses a load-density trend F[MJ/kg] = 0.71 + 7.0e-4*(charge/chamber, kg/m3), RMS ~7% (denser loadings want more effective impetus). Nearly equal to Cordite MD in force despite higher NG (offset by less NC, more inert centralite). T_v 3090 K (external source, cooler than MD 3217 K) sets only the temperature readout.
Web-size estimator (full-bore convention): web[mm] = 20.3*(travel/MV[ms])^1.05 * E^-1.08 * ld^2.83, E = (chamber+bore-swept)/chamber, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]. Leave-one-out CV 8.2% (E and ld a collinear pair). Shared 0.5 mm web floor (defined under SPD) never binds for SC - predictions stay >= 1 mm.
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = charge[kg]/0.45 (loading density ~0.45 kg/dm3, charge exponent ~1, LOO-CV 11%; 15in/42 excluded here as the one gun shared with MD). Exhaustive log-log search (charge, caliber, shell, MV, travel, bore-volume) drops in-sample LOO to ~4-7% only through collinear-ridge multi-term fits (wild opposing exponents e.g. caliber^3.7*MV^-3.4, fragile at n=10) - no robust or physical term improves it. Unlike SPD there is no localized outlier to split out (dropping any single gun leaves LOO 9-12%); the ~11% is genuine distributed scatter across an old heterogeneous fleet. Charge-free fallback: chamber ~ 4.1e-6*caliber[mm]^3.12 (LOO 16%).

Japanese naval cordite DC: moderated double-base based on German RP/C12, cord (solid-cylinder) form. Cord designation = diameter in units of 0.1 mm (36DC = 3.6 mm, 85DC = 8.5 mm, 110DC = 11.0 mm) = model web.
Calibrated full-bore (chi=1.1) against an 8-gun fleet (10cm/65 Type 98 .. 46cm/45 Type 94) with MV + pressure, three with known cords (15.5cm/60 36DC, 35.6cm/45 85DC, 46cm/45 110DC). Force 1.00 MJ/kg, u_1 4.2e-9 (web fit to MV): peak-breech pressure across the fleet sits at mean +3.5%, RMS 8% vs quoted; the 46cm/45 Type 94 flagship lands within -2% on cord and -5% on pressure. 'Moderated' shows up as a low burn-rate coefficient (u_1 4.2e-9, slowest of the cordites vs SC 5.1, MD 9.5), not low energy - force is normal-cordite ~1.0. Pressure data fixes force here: the initial 3-gun fit (force 0.95) over-predicted the wider fleet by ~+14%; the under-charged older guns (35.6cm/45 41st Yr, 41cm/45 3rd Yr) need the higher force to reach MV with realistic cords. The 35.6cm/45 stays an outlier (its 85DC cord runs ~25-30% thicker than the model wants) - likely an older lot or soft figures. T_v ~3000 K (readout only). Density, covolume, theta (0.25), pressure exponent (0.90) from the cordite family.
Web-size estimator (full-bore convention): web[mm] = 3.01*(travel/MV[ms])^0.96 * ld^2.98, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]. Leave-one-out CV 10.3%; the expansion-ratio lever adds little here (full tMV*E*ld -> 9.8%) so it is dropped. Predicts the reliable cords well (15.5cm/60 +5%, 46cm/45 -4%); the 35.6cm/45 calibration outlier is -26%. Shared 0.5 mm web floor never binds (DC webs >= 1.5 mm).
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = 1.86e-7*shell[kg]^0.99*MV[m/s]^2.22 (muzzle-energy form, LOO-CV 2.9%, charge-free) - clearly beats the loading-density rule chamber=charge/0.49 (LOO 10%). Exhaustive search confirms this is a genuine independent pair, NOT a collinearity ridge: corr(shell,MV)=-0.54 here (vs ~0.99 among charge/size/travel), because DC's MV range 710-1000 is decorrelated from caliber. Robust (LOO 3-7% dropping any gun) and no third term improves it (caliber*shell*MV 3.1%).

German tube powder (Roehrenpulver) C/12, Konstruktionsjahr 1912: double-base, ~64% nitrocellulose / 30% nitroglycerin / 6% centralite. TUBE form (SimpleGeometry.TUBE): model web = wall thickness = (D_ext - D_int)/2, so the 18/8 mm tubes used by the capital guns give web 5.0 mm; r2 = tube_length/web (near-neutral burn).
Calibrated TRAVEL convention (length_gun = bore - chamber/chi): these guns run very high load density (0.63-0.77 kg/dm3), so the lumped model is efficient and wants the honest travel geometry, not the full-bore expansion fudge used for low-density cordite. Force 0.96 MJ/kg, u_1 4.1e-9 from five capital guns with known 18/8 tubes (38cm/45, 35.5cm/45, 30.5cm/50, 28.3cm/50, 28.3cm/45): web fit to MV reproduces the real 5.0 mm wall within +/-6% and peak-breech pressure within +/-5%. Full 8-gun fleet (down to 8.8cm/45): pressure mean +5.5%, RMS 9% - the small guns (unknown thin tubes) over-predict ~+14-18% (thin-web bias). T_v ~3000 K (readout). Density, covolume, theta (0.25), n (0.90) from the double-base family.
Web-size estimator (travel convention, predicts tube wall): web[mm] = 3.95*(travel/MV[ms])^1.01 * E^-1.00 * ld^1.72, E = (chamber+bore-swept)/chamber, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]. Leave-one-out CV 2.0% - needs all three levers (E and ld are a suppressor pair; tMV*ld alone ~13%). With only 8 guns the E/ld split is less certain than the larger fleets, but the combined prediction cross-validates well and reproduces the 18/8 wall (5.0 mm) within +/-6% on the capital guns. Shared 0.5 mm web floor never binds (RP C/12 webs >= 1.6 mm).
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = charge[kg]/0.68 (loading density ~0.68 kg/dm3, charge exponent ~1.02, LOO-CV 9%, CV 6.4% - very consistent). Exhaustive search: no term improves it. Notably shell*MV^2 FAILS here (LOO 16%, fragile: drop 14.9cm/45 -> 44%): MV is essentially uncorrelated with size (corr(shell,MV)=+0.21), so it adds no chamber signal. Contrast DC and RP C/32, where small guns are deliberately faster (corr -0.54, -0.74) and shell*MV is genuine - so the discriminator is shell-MV anti-correlation, not MV range (C/32 shares C/12's narrow range yet works). One mild leverage outlier, 14.9cm/45 (ratio 1.58); dropping it gives LOO 4.9%. Charge-free fallback: chamber = 4.2e-8*shell[kg]^1.01*MV[m/s]^2.40 (LOO 16%).

German diglycol tube powder (Gudol) RP C/32, Konstruktionsjahr 1932, with the closely related C/34/C/38: 'cold' low-erosion double-base (nitrocellulose + diethylene-glycol dinitrate) that let WWII Kriegsmarine guns reach 900-960 m/s with long barrel life. TUBE form (SimpleGeometry.TUBE): model web = wall = (D_ext - D_int)/2, e.g. 22/11 -> 5.5, 16/7 -> 4.5, 18/10 -> 4.0, 12/5 -> 3.5, 11/5.75 -> 2.6 mm; r2 = tube_length/web.
Calibrated TRAVEL convention (load density 0.62-0.74, as RP C/12). Force 0.99 MJ/kg, u_1 3.3e-9 (slow-burning, even below C/12's 4.1) from six guns with known tube walls (40.6cm/52 SK C/34 down to 14.9cm/60 SK C/25). Web fit to MV reproduces the real walls within +/-11% and peak-breech pressure to mean -0.3%, RMS 3.7% across the 7-gun fleet (incl 10.5cm/65) - the tightest fit of the custom set. No force split between the C/38 capital guns and the C/32 secondaries. T_v ~2600 K (diglycol is cold; readout only - low flame temp with low-molar-mass products still gives force ~1.0). Density, covolume, theta (0.25), n (0.90) from the family.
Web-size estimator (travel convention, predicts tube wall): web[mm] = 2.41*(travel/MV[ms])^0.99 * E^-0.81 * ld^1.62, E = (chamber+bore-swept)/chamber, ld = charge/chamber [kg/dm3]. Leave-one-out CV 2.9% (full three-lever; here E is the clean second lever, while tMV*ld alone is unstable - tMV and ld collinear at r=-0.85). Reproduces the real tube walls within +/-11% (RMS 6%). With 7 guns the exponents are less certain than the larger fleets. Shared 0.5 mm web floor never binds (RP C/32 webs >= 1.6 mm).
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = 2.25e-10*shell[kg]^1.03*MV[m/s]^3.15 (muzzle-energy form, LOO-CV 4.3%, charge-free) - beats the loading-density rule chamber=charge/0.68 (LOO 7%). Deep check confirms it is genuine (like DC, not a ridge): shell and MV are strongly anti-correlated (corr -0.74, small guns deliberately faster), so MV carries real chamber signal and shell*MV beats charge on 6 of 7 leave-one-out drops. Weaker than DC though - the narrow MV range (810-960) inflates the MV exponent to 3.15 (vs DC 2.22) and the fit is sensitive to the 28cm/52 (drop -> 11.5%); charge (rho 0.68, LOO 7%) is a safe fallback.

RN cordite Mark I (adopted 1889; issued from 1893), the original: 37% nitroglycerin / 58% guncotton / 5% mineral jelly - higher NG than the later 'Modified' MD (30%), so hotter-burning and notoriously erosive, which is exactly why MD was developed. Cord (solid-cylinder) form, full-bore convention, modelled like MD. Cord sizing: 'Cordite N' = extrusion-die diameter N*0.010 in = model web - 3-pdr -> Cordite 5 (1.27 mm), 6in & 9.2in/31.5 -> Cordite 30 (7.62), 9.2in/40 -> Cordite 40 (10.16), 12in Mk VIII/IX -> Cordite 50 (12.70 mm).
Force 1.00 MJ/kg, u_1 9.5e-9, anchored on the 12in/40 Mk IX at its Cordite 50 cord (MV ~790, peak-breech ~265 MPa, sane) - similar to MD in impetus, with the higher NG raising flame temperature (T_v ~3400 K, the erosion driver) more than force. (An earlier same-web cross-calibration over-stated force at 1.20; the real cords disprove it.) The four cord-anchored guns show a MONOTONIC caliber residual - per-gun force runs 1.42 (6in) / 1.28 (9.2in/31.5) / 1.20 (9.2in/40) / 1.02 (12in) at u_1 9.5 - the signature of the lumped model under-burning thick cords in these short pre-dreadnought barrels (a higher u_1 ~15 flattens it), so the big 12in that burns most completely is the unbiased anchor and the smaller guns only appear to want more force. The 9.2in/31.5 Mk III also has an oversized chamber (load density 0.30) originally sized for prismatic brown powder. theta (0.26), density, covolume, n from the MD family.
Web-size estimator (full-bore; only 4 cord-anchored guns, so below the usual 3-lever fit): the universal tMV backbone holds - web[mm] = 0.74*(travel/MV[ms])^1.02 (exponent ~1 as in every propellant, in-sample RMS 9% on the real cords). Load density tightens it to web = 1.13*(travel/MV)^1.09*ld^0.62 (RMS 2.4%, ld pulling down the low-density 9.2in/31.5), but n=4 cannot be cross-validated and the full tMV*E*ld has zero dof. E carries no signal, and the MD estimator does NOT transfer (its E^-1.11*ld^2.03 over-corrects the short small guns, RMS 36%) - estimator exponents are fleet-specific, not just propellant-specific.
Chamber estimator: chamber[dm3] = charge[kg]/0.41 (loading density ~0.41 kg/dm3, ~MD's 0.42; CV 5.3% over the three standard guns). The 9.2in/31.5 Mk III is an oversized-chamber outlier (rho 0.30, brown-powder origin) that inflates a blanket fit to rho 0.37 / CV 15%. No multi-term gain - shell and MV are positively correlated here (corr +0.68, the old-fleet pattern), so shell*MV^2 is a ridge; charge is the only robust predictor, as for SPD/SC/MD.
